name: AddPublishers
title: Publishers become a table
summary: Publishers get their own table, and each book points to its publisher instead of a hand-typed name.

notes.why: The same publisher was typed in many ways (« Gallimard », « gallimard », « Gallimard  »). A table gives one row per publisher, and books can be listed by publisher.
notes.compatibility: `book.publisher_name` stays in place and is still filled by the current version of the application, which does not know `publisher_id` yet. Nothing breaks during the deployment.
notes.deployment:
1. Apply the migration: it creates the publishers from the names already typed and links the books.
2. Deploy the application that writes `publisher_id`.
notes.deferred: `book.publisher_name` is dropped by a later migration, once no running version writes it any more (see `DropPublisherName`).

addReferences.name: book_publisher
addReferences.description: Deleting a publisher keeps its books, without publisher.

data.description: One publisher is created per distinct name already typed (spaces trimmed), and each book is linked to it. Running it again creates nothing new.
data.up:
INSERT INTO publisher (name)
SELECT DISTINCT btrim(publisher_name) FROM book
WHERE publisher_name IS NOT NULL AND btrim(publisher_name) <> ''
ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING;

UPDATE book b SET publisher_id = p.id
FROM publisher p
WHERE p.name = btrim(b.publisher_name) AND b.publisher_id IS NULL;
